newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks seen starting higher.
newsitem.headline: French stocks seen starting higher.

text.p: French shares were expected to open in positive ground, with bullish sentiment and liquidity giving support, traders said.

"The only way is up," said a broker, citing a catch-up by Paris which has lagged other bourses, and the July 15 maturing of the "Balladur bond" which is expected to bring retail savings into the stock market.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 26.20 points or 0.91 percent at 2,893.64. The CAC-40 futures contract on GLOBEX was up eight at 2,902 from Thursday's close.
Monday sees the expiry of June futures and options contracts, which should further boost volumes.
The Paris market appears to be playing down the overnight weaker close on Wall Street and pursuing its own destiny, brokers said.

Comments by Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn on Thursday that France o:Par s:rwswould miss the three percent target Maastricht target for public deficits did not pose major concern. "We know that no country will meet the strict interpretation, not even Germany, so it suits everyone," said a trader. -- Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452
